message.content:
LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes in the history of the sport. Born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, he rose to prominence as a high school phenom at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School, where he was named the USA Today High School Player of the Year and led his team to a state championship.

He entered the NBA directly from high school in 2003, being selected first overall by the Cleveland Cavaliers. LeBron quickly became known for his combination of size, athleticism, court vision, and scoring ability. He has won multiple NBA championships (2012, 2013, 2016, 2020) with the Miami Heat, Cleveland Cavaliers, and Los Angeles Lakers, earning Finals MVP honors each time. In addition to his club success, he has been selected to numerous All‑NBA teams, earned several regular‑season MVP awards, and represented the United States in international competition, winning Olympic gold medals in 2008, 2012, and 2016.

Off the court, LeBron is also recognized for his philanthropy—most notably the opening of the “I Promise School” in Akron—and his ventures into media and entertainment, including production deals and his own network, Uninterrupted.
